title: Defensive Programming and Input Validation
learningObjectives: Describe the main idea and its role in reliable program behavior.
Recognize the topic in code or a real-world programming scenario.
Trace the relevant behavior and identify the likely outcome.
Explain a common mistake, risk, or limitation.
Apply the concept and verify the result with a suitable check.

understand.concept: Defensive programming anticipates invalid, unexpected, incomplete, or hostile inputs and protects assumptions at boundaries. Validation checks that data has the expected type, range, shape, and meaning before it is used. Validation should be specific, consistent, and appropriate to the risk; client-side checks improve usability but server-side validation remains necessary for trusted decisions.
understand.whyItMatters: Inputs from users, files, APIs, devices, and other systems are not automatically trustworthy. Validating at boundaries prevents invalid state, confusing failures, and security vulnerabilities.
understand.analogy: A building checks a visitor's badge and access area before allowing entry. A badge alone is not enough if the rules or destination are wrong. Software validates data against the operation it will perform.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a simplified comparison; software failures and recovery depend on language, runtime, system boundaries, and context.

explain.narrative: Define what valid input means before coding. Check type, required presence, length, format, range, and domain rules as needed. Reject or safely normalize invalid values, communicate actionable feedback, and validate again on the trusted server for security-sensitive operations.

examples.explanation: Validation combines integer type and acceptable bounds.

examples.title: Allow-list choice
examples.explanation: An allow-list is safer than accepting arbitrary values.

examples.title: Validate array shape
examples.explanation: Check collection type and item types before processing.

examples.title: Boundary validation
examples.explanation: Boundary checks reject values outside the documented range.

commonMistakes: Validating only in the browser for security-sensitive operations.
Using vague checks that allow unexpected values.
Silently changing invalid data without telling the user.
Forgetting type, range, size, and domain constraints.
Trusting data after it crosses another system boundary.

Test normal, invalid, and boundary cases and record the result.

independentTask.title: Independent practice: Defensive Programming and Input Validation
independentTask.instructions: Create a small original program or pseudocode scenario applying this topic.
requirements: Implement the topic with clear behavior.
Include at least one normal case and one failure or edge case.
Show the observed output or test result.

hints: Start by defining expected behavior precisely.
Inspect the earliest relevant failure or boundary.
Make one change at a time and retest.
Keep user-facing messages useful and safe.
Verify both normal and failure paths.

questions.prompt: Where should input validation usually occur?
options: At trust boundaries before data is used
Only after the data is saved
questions.answer: At trust boundaries before data is used
questions.explanation: Validate untrusted or externally sourced data before relying on it.

Whether a variable has a nice name
Whether a user clicked a button
questions.answer: Whether a value falls within permitted limits
questions.explanation: Range checks ensure numeric values stay within expected boundaries.

questions.prompt: Why is client-side validation not sufficient for security?
options: Users can bypass or alter client-side checks
questions.answer: Users can bypass or alter client-side checks
questions.explanation: Server-side checks are needed for trusted decisions.

questions.prompt: Which is safer for a limited set of choices?
options: An explicit allow-list of valid options
questions.answer: An explicit allow-list of valid options
questions.explanation: Allow-lists constrain values to known acceptable choices.

questions.prompt: What is a good validation strategy?
options: Define expected type, format, range, and meaning based on risk
Check only whether a field is nonempty
questions.answer: Define expected type, format, range, and meaning based on risk
questions.explanation: Validation should cover the constraints relevant to the operation.
